sophie (devex): Heads-up from today's onboarding lab: new users hitting silent workspace mixups because the runtime prefers cached keyring tokens over explicit env vars.

raj (sdk): that's bad. Which env names were involved?

sophie (devex): quickstart uses REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY in docs but my shell had REDWOOD_ORG_KEY set. The container image used the helper lib which read the keyring first and returned the org key.

emma (platform): ugh. loader order should be: explicit env -> keyring -> metadata. Any snippet you can paste?

sophie (devex): tiny excerpt from helper: `const token = keyring.get('rw:token') || process.env.REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_ORG_KEY` that's the root cause.

raj (sdk): ok we need a two-part fix: 1) flip precedence to prefer env vars, 2) stop using a single `rw:token` id in keyring. Namespacing is required.

olga (security): +1 and add audit logging for any write to keyring. Also require explicit confirmation for rotating org-scoped credentials interactively.

emma (platform): propose namespaced ids like `rw:org:<org_id>:token` and `rw:project:<proj_id>:token`. Also a startup warning if an org token is present in keyring but project env var is set. Something like: `WARN: org token found in keyring while REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY is set; using REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY` with link to docs.

sophie (devex): can we add a tiny CLI lint that fails Docker builds if it sees REDWOOD_ORG_KEY or similar in the Dockerfile? Many users accidentally bake org keys into images.

build-bot: issue #1542 created: add Dockerfile/CI check for org-scoped envs. Assigned to emma.

raj (sdk): I'll open a patch to flip loader order and add unit tests for combinations: only org env, only project env, both envs, keyring only, env+keyring. Also add keyring API change to include namespace.

olga (security): please include migration guidance for developers who already have `rw:token` in their keyring. We need a small migration tool to move existing entries to namespaced keys safely.

emma (platform): noted. I'll draft a migration script and a short how-to: detect old keys, re-register under project/org namespace, optionally delete the legacy entry.

sophie (devex): UX suggestion: when both envs are set, print a clear one-line message at startup: `Both REDWOOD_ORG_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY set; using REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (recommended)`. That was the exact confusion for my workshop attendees.

raj (sdk): implemented in branch flip-env-precedence-314. Also added `REDWOOD_AUTH_STRICT=1` as an opt-in mode that enforces token scope matching and fails fast if mismatch detected. Tests included.

build-bot: CI: branch flip-env-precedence-314 passed unit tests; integration matrix pending.

olga (security): good. Also make sure rotate tools never write to legacy unscoped key ids. And add audit trail entries for rotate operations.

emma (platform): after merge I'll update the quickstart Dockerfile to `ENV REDWOOD_ORG_KEY=\"\"` in the example and publish a short upgrade note for partners.

sophie (devex): thanks all. This will stop a lot of painful "why is my demo billed to someone else's org" moments. I'll close once PR merged and quickstart image rebuilt. :white_check_mark:
